claims.text: The Interface Segregation Principle: no client should be forced to depend on methods it does not use; many small, client-specific interfaces are better than one general-purpose interface.
claims.source_hint: glossary entry isp; standard formulation in software design literature

claims.text: In C#, a non-abstract class that implements an interface must provide every member of that interface, otherwise it fails to compile (CS0535).
claims.source_hint: C# compiler error CS0535; C# interfaces docs

claims.text: If an interface method's parameters change, every class implementing that interface must change its implementation to keep compiling.
claims.source_hint: C# interfaces: implementing members must match the interface member signature

claims.text: INotifier declares exactly one member: void Send(int orderId, string subject).
NotifierBase implements INotifier: its Send formats the message, adds it to a private sent list exposed as Sent, and prints it; Format is abstract. EmailNotifier and SmsNotifier override only Format.
Nothing in the samples at stage-0 tracks message delivery; INotificationChannel and GetDeliveryReport are hypothetical.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-0: git grep -i delivery samples/

claims.text: A filler implementation that throws breaks substitutability: callers holding the interface may call that method and cannot know this implementation fails.
claims.source_hint: follows from LSP (previous lesson) and outline item 3

claims.text: Method count is a symptom; ISP is about whether each implementer and caller needs every method it is forced to depend on.

self_check.notes: EmailNotifier/SmsNotifier implement INotifier through NotifierBase and override only Format; NotifierBase.cs added to example_files and outline item 2 reworded to match. INotificationChannel is hypothetical, prose only. No Adapter/role-interface terms, per depth_notes.
